answer: Seat prompts walk a public trellis of templates, but each path is keyed by the identity's pubkey and a beacon of fresh entropy, so two heads never share a branch and a clone's output stays a mirror of its parent until it re-runs inference on its own path. Every answer commits to the branch it walked; the auditor fires a gale of re-derivations at random seats, and if the commitment mismatches the seat voids. Divergence costs one full generation per head, non-poolable, so a farm pays it k times.
